title: Lost GET — Reporting and Recovery
body: One missed tooth that rides a truck to the ROM pad and into the primary crusher turns into liner damage, hours of plant downtime, and a jammed-liner repair that's a safety event in its own right. At ADW the cost of stopping the dig for ten minutes is always smaller than the cost of letting a lost tooth pass through — the whole procedure exists to make sure crews act on that math in the moment, not after the fact.
keyPoints: Stop first, every time. Any suspected GET loss means the equipment stops immediately — no "finish the pass and check after."
Report with specifics: equipment ID, operator, GPS location, and exactly what and how many pieces are missing, notified to Survey, Drill & Blast, Load & Haul, and Safety together.
Recovery is controlled, not a scramble — visual search, GPS-pinpointed digging, and material tracked to wherever it ends up (pit, stockpile, ROM pad, crusher) if it isn't found on the spot.
If it's not recovered before the material moves on, the loader operator feeding the crusher is the last line of defense — every load gets eyeballed for the missing piece at the ROM pad.

Prevention beats recovery: pre-start and daily GET checks, full documentation on every change-out (including single-tooth swaps), and operators trained to recognize the feel and sound of a lost tooth or lip.
apply: Any excavator or loader working a fresh muck pile after blasting — a lost tooth in broken rock is far easier to miss than one on a clean floor, so that's where a stop-and-check habit pays off.
